about: What the SFX parity packs ship, and what was tried: per shipped cue the pick, its provenance (the exact request body, the character-cost the service reported, sha256 of the raw take and of the mastered file) and its measured level against the row. 'set' says how the pick passed: 'strict' (every check the spec holds a take to), 'near' (attack, centroid and bands each within 1.5 times the tolerance: the driver's call of 2026-10-12 installs the loose set, strict plus near, and Bailey's ear decides), or 'driver' (the second batch, 2026-10-13: the best take of a row that is neither, which the driver marked 'use the new take' on the listening page after hearing its measured distance from the row beside today's cue; 'fit' and 'deviations' say how far it is, where 1.0 is the edge of the spec's tolerance, and 'levelFlags' marks a take that was mastered below its row's level because a limiter would have had to take more than 3 dB). 47 cues ship. 'rejected' keeps the takes measurement turned down (272 of the 2026-10-13 run, with the checks they failed, and the pilot's one), so the same prompt is not paid for twice; a take that now ships is not listed there. Agents cannot hear (rule 13): every pick is by measurement against the spec row and stays open to Bailey's ear. Numbers and our own takes only; no retail id, name or audio is recorded here.
